Tolerance for benchmark noise: 5 percent of the anchor's score (the evaluations used publish no interval in our data); the minimum is the anchor's score times (1 - tolerance).

Form (replaces the first two forms, both written after rankings were seen): the first used a floor relative to the best eligible arm, which let the strongest model push the next one out; the second used hand-set absolute minimums, which are guesses on benchmark scales we do not own and again selected the top model on a one-provider install. This form anchors each minimum to the tier's held default, so the question is whether a model at least as good as what works today is cheaper or faster: score = cost_factor^wc x speed_factor^ws x (1 + bonus x capability_share) among arms that clear every anchored minimum. The held default always clears its own minimum, so a tier never moves to a dearer model merely because a stronger one exists. An evaluation on which the anchor has no current number is dropped from the minimums and the capability share and listed as missing, never guessed. Best has no minimum.
